procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came back as promised. Rash faded over Dec-Jan, joints better, urine lighter. Still tired by end of a work day. Feet the same - tingling, not worse.
We spent most of the visit on ART. He's more open than before - asked what the pill is, how often labs would be, whether he'd have to see a specialist. Answered all of it. He wants to "get through the winter jobs" first. Not a no. Gave written info and the HIV clinic number again.
Exam: no purpura, joints quiet, vibration reduced distally.
Labs: BMP, UA, CBC. Continue TMP-SMX DS three times weekly - says he's been better about it since the November talk.
RTC early summer (video ok).

documents.title: TMP-SMX Refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy e-request TMP-SMX 800/160 #36. Fill history looks on time since Nov. Approved with 3 refills.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from his truck after work, identity verified. Summer's been fine. No rash, joints OK, no fever, no cough, eating normally. Feet unchanged. Taking Bactrim.
ART - says he looked at the paper, "still nervous about it." Gently pushed; he'll decide by his physical. 
No changes. Physical with labs in Sept.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam, 49M.
No illnesses since spring. Cryo symptoms quiet through summer as usual. Energy fair. No fevers, sweats, cough, weight loss, diarrhea, oral sores.
Meds unchanged; NKDA. Former smoker, rare alcohol, same work.
Exam: weight stable. Oropharynx clear. No nodes. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft. Skin clear. Reduced vibration toes. R knee crepitus.
A/P: prevention - flu, COVID today; FIT kit; MenACWY booster due next fall. Labs: CMP, CBC, urine albumin, CD4/VL. ART: told me "after the holidays, for real." Will hold him to it at a Feb/March visit.

documents.title: Refill and Scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called for Bactrim refill (routed to RN, sent) and to book the follow-up the doctor asked for after New Year. Booked Mon 3/9 7:40 am - earliest he can do with the job schedule.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
50M, advanced HIV off ART, HIV-associated cryoglobulinemia, CKD 2.
S: No rash on his legs now. Joints stiff mornings. Feet tingle, stable. No fever, cough, weight change, mouth sores. Bactrim most weeks. 
ART: we had the conversation he promised. He is closer - asked to see the CD4 and viral load from today first and then "probably" start. I'll send results and a plan; can start through us or the HIV clinic, his choice.
O: Afebrile, vitals fine, weight 76ish. Mouth clear. No nodes. Lungs clear. RRR. No purpura. Reduced vibration toes.
A/P: labs as above. Continue TMP-SMX DS three times weekly, ibuprofen/APAP prn. Follow up in about 6 months, sooner once he decides on ART.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Todd - CD4 is lower again and the viral load higher than last fall. Kidney function and blood count are stable. This is the moment I'd pick to start. If you message me back yes, I'll set up the HIV clinic intake or start it here, whichever you want.

documents.title: RE: Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Let me get through this month on the job and I'll call. thanks

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
OUTSIDE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Date of visit: 05/06/2026

CC: cough and fever x3 weeks; painful lump right forearm.
HPI: 50M with advanced HIV not on antiretroviral therapy, asplenic, on TMP-SMX prophylaxis (reports missed doses). Three weeks of productive cough, fevers and weight loss. About a week ago noticed what he thought was a pimple on the right forearm; it has since grown into a tender swollen lump.
PMH: HIV/AIDS, cryoglobulinemia, CKD 2, anemia of chronic disease, peripheral neuropathy. PSH: bilateral femur ORIF and splenectomy after 2011 MVC.
Meds: TMP-SMX DS three times weekly, ibuprofen prn, acetaminophen prn. Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals on arrival: T 38.2 C (100.8 F), BP 125/80, RR 22.
Exam: ill-appearing, speaking full sentences. Scattered crackles right base. Right forearm: single fluctuant, erythematous, tender nodule. No other skin lesions. Neuro nonfocal, alert and oriented.
Results: WBC 9.0, Hgb 12.5, CD4 120. Sputum Gram stain: filamentous gram-positive rods, weakly acid-fast. CXR: patchy RLL infiltrates.

ED course / impression: pulmonary nocardiosis with a cutaneous (forearm) lesion in advanced HIV. Infectious disease consulted by phone. Admitted to medicine.

- Emergency Medicine

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/06/2026 via the emergency department. Discharged 05/09/2026.

Diagnoses: pulmonary nocardiosis; cutaneous nocardiosis, right forearm (HIV-related opportunistic skin infection); advanced HIV, not on ART.

Course: admitted with three weeks of cough, fever and weight loss and a fluctuant right forearm nodule; sputum smear showed filamentous gram-positive, weakly acid-fast rods and the culture grew Nocardia species. Defervesced within 48 hours on treatment-dose trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Forearm lesion smaller and less tender at discharge. Breathing comfortably on room air.

Discharge medications:
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS (800/160 mg), 2 tablets by mouth twice daily, planned for at least 6 months (replaces the three-times-weekly prophylaxis dose)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed
- Ibuprofen 400 mg every 6 hours as needed (home medication, continued)
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Follow-up: infectious disease clinic appointment arranged; antiretroviral therapy to be started there. Primary care follow-up advised.

- Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Outside Records Filed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED record and discharge summary received and filed. RN calling him.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt after hearing of his admission (ED record arrived yesterday). Home since Sat, feels better, fever gone, cough easing, forearm less sore. Has the new Bactrim dose - 2 tabs twice a day - and understands it's for months. Knows about an ID clinic appointment but couldn't say the date; asked him to find the card and call them. Offered a visit with PCP; he'd rather wait until he's back to work. Told to call for fever, headache, confusion or worse breathing.

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Right lower lobe airspace infiltrate. Left lung clear. No effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal.

reports.study: MRI brain, with and without gadolinium
reports.text: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain before and after IV gadolinium. Single 1.6 cm ring-enhancing lesion in the right frontal lobe with mild surrounding vasogenic edema. No midline shift. No hydrocephalus. No other enhancing lesions. No acute infarct or hemorrhage.
reports.conclusion: Single 1.6 cm ring-enhancing right frontal lesion with mild edema and no midline shift, consistent with abscess (nocardial in this clinical setting).

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care medicine
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 07/13/2026 (ICU, then medical floor). Discharged 08/11/2026.

Principal diagnosis: nocardiosis, pulmonary with central nervous system involvement (right frontal brain abscess).
Other: advanced HIV/AIDS, antiretroviral therapy started this admission; HIV-associated cryoglobulinemia; CKD stage 2; anemia of chronic disease; peripheral neuropathy; asplenia.

Presentation: 50-year-old man treated for pulmonary and cutaneous nocardiosis two months ago, who stopped his oral antibiotic after a few weeks. Two weeks of cough, fever and increasing breathlessness, with a severe headache and spells of confusion. On arrival T 38.9 C, BP 110/70, HR 102, RR 22. Crackles at the right base; mildly disoriented to time and place, no focal weakness. WBC 12.0, Hgb 13.2, platelets 250, CD4 50 cells/mm3, HIV viral load 120,000 copies/mL. CXR right lower lobe infiltrate. Sputum Gram stain with branching filamentous organisms; culture grew Nocardia species. MRI brain: single 1.6 cm ring-enhancing right frontal lesion, mild edema, no shift.

Course: ICU for close neurologic monitoring. IV trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole plus IV imipenem. Headache and confusion resolved over the first week; transferred to the floor. Infectious disease started bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 50/200/25 mg daily on 07/28. Tolerating all medications at discharge, oriented, ambulating, on room air.

Discharge medications:
- Bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 50/200/25 mg, 1 tablet daily
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS (800/160 mg), 2 tablets by mouth three times daily, for at least 12 months
- Acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Follow-up: infectious disease clinic in 2 weeks, with repeat brain MRI and labs arranged by ID. Primary care within 4 weeks.

- Critical Care / Hospital Medicine

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Discharge summary received and filed. He'll need a visit soon - front desk to reach him.

documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I was in the hospital again for most of July. I'm home now and on the HIV pill finally plus the big Bactrim dose. Hospital said to see you within a month. Mornings are best. Thanks

documents.body: Glad you're home, Todd. You're booked Tuesday 9/8 at 8:00 am with your doctor. Please bring all your pill bottles.
